question: What change in accounting estimate did Microsoft make in July 2020, and what was its effect on FY2021 results?
gold_answer: It extended the useful life of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years. This raised operating income by $2.7 billion and net income by $2.3 billion, or $0.30 per basic and diluted share. (Page 41, Item 7)

question: What were the terms of Microsoft’s agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, and when was it expected to close?

question: What role does Azure play for OpenAI, according to Microsoft’s FY2023 10-K?
gold_answer: Microsoft says Azure is OpenAI’s exclusive cloud provider and powers all of OpenAI’s workloads. It also says it increased its investment in supercomputing systems to accelerate OpenAI’s research. The risk-factors section separately mentions that in January 2023 Microsoft announced the third phase of its OpenAI strategic partnership.

question: What was the “Q2 charge” in fiscal 2023, what did it consist of, and how many jobs were cut?
gold_answer: It was a $1.2 billion charge in Q2 FY2023, announced January 18, 2023. It included $800 million of employee severance, impairment charges from changes to the hardware portfolio, and lease-consolidation costs. Microsoft reduced its workforce by about 10,000 jobs through Q3 FY2023, which is less than 5% of its employee base.

question: What was the status of the Activision Blizzard acquisition in the FY2023 10-K?
gold_answer: It was still pending. The deal is $95.00 per share, all cash, valued at $68.7 billion. Microsoft and Activision Blizzard had jointly agreed to extend the merger agreement through October 18, 2023 to resolve remaining regulatory concerns. This differs from the FY2022 filing, which said the deal was expected to close in fiscal year 2023.
source_note: MSFT_FY2023_10K.pdf, PDF p.54 (printed p.52); the FY2022 comparison is in MSFT_FY2022_10K.pdf, p.52

question: What did Microsoft ultimately pay for Activision Blizzard, and when did the deal close?
gold_answer: It closed on October 13, 2023 at a total purchase price of $75.4 billion, consisting primarily of cash (Note 8 shows $75,408M). That is higher than the $68.7 billion announced price quoted in the FY2022 and FY2023 filings. Xbox content and services revenue rose 50%, with 44 points coming from the net impact of the acquisition.
source_note: MSFT_FY2024_10K.pdf, PDF p.56 (printed p.39) and PDF p.109 (Note 8). The $68.7B comparison is in MSFT_FY2023_10K.pdf, PDF p.54.

question: What agreement did Microsoft make with Inflection AI in March 2024, and why is it disclosed as a related-party transaction?
gold_answer: Microsoft obtained a non-exclusive license to Inflection’s intellectual property. It is a related-party item because Reid Hoffman, a Microsoft board member, is a co-founder of Inflection and sits on its board. Reprogrammed Interchange LLC and entities affiliated with Greylock Ventures (both linked to Hoffman) each held less than 10% of Inflection at the time. He did not participate in the board’s review of the deal.

question: What was Microsoft’s effective tax rate in FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024, and why did it fall in FY2024?
gold_answer: The rates were 13%, 19% and 18%. The FY2024 decrease came mainly from tax law changes: IRS Notice 2023-55 (Q1 FY2024) delayed the effective date of the final foreign tax credit regulations to FY2024 for Microsoft, and Notice 2023-80 (Q2 FY2024) delayed it indefinitely.
source_note: MSFT_FY2024_10K.pdf, PDF p.68 (printed p.47) for 18% and 19%. MSFT_FY2023_10K.pdf, PDF p.50 for 19% and 13%.

question: what are some of the latest intellectual property risks for Microsoft?
gold_answer: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RISKS We face risks related to the protection and utilization of our intellectual property that may result in our business and operating results being harmed. Protecting our intellectual property rights and combating unlicensed copying and use of our software, source code, trade secrets, and other intellectual property on a global basis is difficult. Similarly, the absence of harmonized patent laws makes it more difficult to ensure consistent respect for patent rights. Source code, the detailed program commands for our software programs, is critical to our business. Unauthorized access to or disclosure of source code or other intellectual property may negatively impact future trade secret protection for that intellectual property. It may then become easier for third parties to compete with our products by copying functionality, which could adversely affect our results of operations. Unauthorized access to or disclosure of source code or other intellectual property also increases the security risks described elsewhere in these risk factors. Third parties may claim that we infringe their intellectual property. From time to time, others claim we infringe their intellectual property rights, including current copyright infringement and other claims arising from AI training, inference, and output. To resolve these claims, we may enter into royalty-bearing data access or licensing agreements on terms that are less favorable than currently available, stop selling or redesign affected products or services, or pay damages to satisfy indemnification commitments with our customers. Adverse outcomes could also include monetary damages or injunctive relief that may limit or prevent importing, marketing, and selling our products or services that have infringing technologies. We have paid significant amounts to settle claims related to the use of technology and intellectual property rights and to procure intellectual property rights as part of our strategy to manage this risk, and may continue to do so, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

question: compare Fiscal Year 2026 Compared with Fiscal Year 2025 in terms of revenue
gold_answer: Revenue increased $50.1 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. More Personal Computing revenue decreased driven by XBOX (formerly Gaming), offset in part by growth in Search advertising. Cost of revenue increased $18.5 billion or 21% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Gross margin increased $31.6 billion or 16% with growth across each of our segments. • Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains across the Microsoft Cloud. • Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 66% driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. Operating expenses increased $4.9 billion or 7% driven by continued investments in research and development compute capacity, AI talent, and data to support product development that benefits the entire portfolio, impairment and other related expenses in our XBOX business, investments in commercial sales, and higher Copilot advertising expenses. Operating income increased $26.7 billion or 21% driven by growth in Productivity and Business Processes and Intelligent Cloud. Revenue and operating income both included a favorable foreign currency impact of 2%. (Pg 57)
